name: spinner
behavior: APG progressbar pattern in its indeterminate form (role=progressbar with an accessible name and no aria-valuenow, wrapped in or paired with a polite live region so the busy state is announced; never focusable, never a tab stop; when a spinner stands in for a region's content that region carries aria-busy=true; the rotation is decorative — under prefers-reduced-motion it degrades to a static or fading indicator and the announcement carries the meaning)

parts.note: the busy element that carries role and accessible name; sized by the icon ramp, coloured by the surrounding content role
the sweeping arc drawn on a border-subtle track; the arc takes the action colour so a spinner reads as the same 'system is working' voice as a primary action

anatomyNotes: Intersection of shadcn Spinner (a single Loader2 icon spun by a utility — track and arc fused into one glyph path) and Salt Spinner (an explicit SVG with a separate track ring and rotating arc, plus an aria-announcer that re-announces on an interval). Two parts is the honest intersection: shadcn's glyph collapses them visually but both are present, and splitting them is what lets a theme choose whether the track is visible. Size binds to the icon ramp (icon-size-inline / control / emphasis), NOT to control-height-* — a spinner is a glyph, not a control. The only state is loading: a spinner that is not loading does not exist, it unmounts. Salt's announcer interval is a behavior detail of the same APG contract, not extra anatomy.
